editorial:
Ever wonder why every single movie today feels like a giant event with toys and huge sets? You should dive into this documentary because it takes you back to 1989 to see how Tim Burton changed the game. It focuses on the making of the first big Batman movie and shows how it turned a comic book character into a global goldmine. The vibe is like a nostalgic trip through old movie studios, filled with great clips and stories from people who were actually there. It makes you realize that before this film, superhero movies were mostly just cheesy TV shows or low-budget flicks.

What really works here is the pacing; it never feels like a boring history lesson. The best part is seeing the behind-the-scenes struggle to get the dark look of Gotham City just right. While it might be a bit short for some, it gives you exactly what you need to understand modern cinema.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by showing how the success of Batman paved the way for the Marvel and DC movies we see today. It explains that the huge amount of merchandise and marketing used back then became the blueprint for every big franchise now. The final scenes show that without Tim Burton's risky choices, the modern blockbuster might not even exist. It ends on a high note, proving that art and big business can actually work together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves superhero movies and movie history.
